editorial:
Imagine walking down a city street and seeing the giant ads on the walls suddenly wake up and start dancing. That is exactly what happens here in this wacky short. You get to meet Eddie Camphor and his buddy Rub-Him-Off, who plays a funny instrument called a wioleen. They take over the scene with a catchy song and dance to a rewritten version of Merrily We Roll Along. The whole thing feels like a colorful, chaotic party where the rules of reality do not apply, making it a quick blast of old-school fun that does not take itself too seriously.

The animation is snappy and the timing of the jokes hits just right for a classic cartoon. You will love how the characters bounce around the screen, though some of the humor is very specific to the 1930s. If you enjoy seeing where modern animation started, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: The chaos reaches a peak as the billboard characters finish their big musical number. After all the singing and dancing, the magic wears off and the characters return to their flat, painted positions on the walls. The twist is simply that the world goes back to normal as if nothing happened. You are left with the funny image of the billboards looking frozen again, leaving the city quiet once more.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic cartoons and musical comedy.
